market_notes.notes: The core environment themes in this cluster are saturated on Fab. Search turned up many large modular castle kits: Medieval Castle with 305 meshes, Medieval Kingdom with 580 meshes and a wall spline tool, Castle Forge, Ravenhold, and Modular Castle & Dungeon with 945 meshes. There are also at least 7 Viking village megapacks (Modular Viking Village with 178 meshes, Viking Village Environment Megapack, VIKINGS Megapack, Medieval Nordic Village), plus about 10 tavern packs, dungeon kits and PCG village and farm generators (Medieval Farmstead Builder, Calysto Village, Farmlands). A solo developer should not compete on another kit of walls and houses. Props and weapons with a small twist are also crowded. I found 5+ listings each for siege weapons (one from KitBash3D), blacksmith forges with interactive Blueprints, carts and wagons, alchemy labs, animated chests, crossbows with reload animations, torches with Blueprints, war-camp tents, shields and Viking weapon packs. Magic spell Niagara packs are heavily crowded, including free ones. Demand for the genre is strong. Articles from 2026 describe medieval games as 'all the rage' (Kingdom Come 2, Manor Lords), Valheim has sold 12M+, and a 'fresh wave' of Norse titles spans survival, city-builders and strategy. Synty's Vikings, Knights, Dungeon and Fantasy Kingdom lines are staple packs. Fab's own review names medieval and fantasy as top themes and says Blueprint-driven products sell. The thin spots are function-layer add-ons that plug into the many existing environment kits. Buyers own castle and village kits but lack working pieces: ships you can drive, gatehouses that open, faction heraldry systems, puzzle wiring, and small hard-surface kitbash like iron hardware. None of these showed a dedicated competitor in 2+ searches. I did not see any prices, review counts or sales numbers for Fab listings (fab.com is not fetchable), apart from one ArtStation price ($35 for the jousting arena kit).

The core cyberpunk and sci-fi staples on Fab are saturated. Cyberpunk city kits alone include Cyberpunk City (260+ meshes, procedural building BPs), Stylized Cyberpunk City (1,003 assets), Cyber Night City (221 pieces), Cyberpunk District, Modular CyberPunk City and a Cyberpunk MEGApack. There are also at least 8 cyberpunk apartment interiors and 5+ neon-sign packs (Neon Signs 2 has 157 BP signs). Sci-fi interiors are just as full (Big Modular SciFi Interior, Modular Sci-Fi Interior I/II and Bundle, a 250-part spaceship/colony pack), and so are space-station kits (5+). Mechs (Mech Constructor Humanoid/Heavy, Mecha Mixer at $29.99 per volume, Modular Mech Weapons), drones (10+), hologram Niagara VFX (5+), hacking systems (HackSkills, Hacking Pack, HackForge), door/keycard BPs, spline cable/pipe kits, hover vehicles (including a full Hoverbike System), sci-fi melee packs and modular sci-fi guns are all crowded. The thin spots are in the retro-futurist sub-genres and in function layers. Dieselpunk on Fab is dominated by KitBash3D's DieselPunk, a cinematic high-poly kit (17.8M polys, no LODs) that was given away free in Nov 2025, so a game-ready dieselpunk kit is thin. Atompunk/raygun weapons turned up only single low-poly pistols. Solarpunk listings are almost all stylized. No salvage/shipbreaking system turned up. On the demand side, co-op extraction horror (Lethal Company, R.E.P.O., Species: Unknown) is described as the fastest-growing indie horror genre on Steam in 2026, and salvage-themed sci-fi games (Ostranauts, Decaying Salvage, The Last Salvage Squad) keep appearing. Synty's POLYGON Sci-Fi Cyber City shows 4.11/5 from 19 reviews on its store, so even big low-poly cyber packs have modest review counts. Most prices and review counts on Fab were not visible in snippets (not seen).

This cluster is one of the most crowded on Fab, so any new product needs either something to do in-game or a specific era or niche. Searches turned up at least 10 listings each for these art-only categories: post-apocalyptic cities and towns (Post Apocalyptic Town, Post Apocalypse City, Modular Post-apocalyptic City, Bunker Builder, Modular Abandoned Factory), wrecked and rusty cars (Destroyed Cars Vol 1, PostApo Car Wrecks, Apocalypse - Vehicles and more), survival prop packs, modular guns and gunsmith systems, drones and FPV drones, pipe and cable spline tools, warehouses, parking garages, rooftop props, subway stations, military bases and FOBs, barriers and HESCO sets, and driveable construction vehicles. Synty's stylized POLYGON Apocalypse ($349.99, 1,800+ prefabs) and POLYGON Military/Apocalypse Wasteland lead the low-poly end. Demand is real and current. Extraction shooters dominated early 2026 Steam (ARC Raiders, Marathon on 2026-03-05, Escape from Duckov). Open World Survival Craft was 2025's "easiest hit genre", with 20.8% of its releases reaching the review milestone (howtomarketagame). Photoreal tactical shooters (Bodycam, Ready or Not on consoles in July 2025) show appetite for close-quarters (CQB) and trench content. Fab has many modern drone listings (Kamikaze Drone, a RAM-2X model, a jet loitering munition, Advanced Drone System with an FPV kamikaze mode). Buyers want present-day drone warfare, but almost every trench kit found is WW1/WW2-era, and no counter-drone or electronic-warfare (EW) gameplay turned up. The gaps are in the function layer: breaching, raid interactables, counter-drone, and vehicle upfit parts that bolt onto any vehicle. These are mechanics that exist only in pieces, or as full templates without matching realistic art. No Fab prices, review counts or listing totals were visible in search snippets (fab.com cannot be fetched), so all competitor prices are "not seen". The session's web-search budget ran out after about 40 queries, so a few gap ratings below rest on 2 queries rather than more.

Horror is one of the most crowded art categories on Fab. Every obvious environment theme came back with 4 to 10 direct Fab listings: asylums and hospitals (Prison and abandoned horror asylum, Asylum Modular Pack, Modular Hospital, Horror Environments Bundle), backrooms and liminal spaces (at least 7 kits, including a Backroom Megapack 1 and 2 and a Liminal Hotel), liminal parking garages (at least 9), gothic and Victorian interiors (Gothic Interior Megapack with 400 assets, Modular Victorian Interior Mansion, Victorian House Interior Collection with 300+ models), cemeteries (at least 8), morgues, torture dungeons, alchemy labs, Halloween (at least 8, including a 370-asset cozy pack) and PSX retro horror. The horror function layer is just as crowded. There are 6+ horror frameworks and templates (Horror Engine SE, Modular Horror System, Horror Mechanics, Analog Horror Template), 8+ CCTV systems, 6+ VHS/CRT post-process packs, lock/keypad puzzle packs and flicker-light systems. So another 'abandoned X' environment or generic horror template is unlikely to be noticed. The demand signal that stands out for 2026 is co-op and extraction horror: Lethal Company, R.E.P.O. (a physics-carry valuables loop) and UE5 extraction-horror titles like FEEDERS are described as the fastest-growing indie horror sub-genre on Steam. My searches found grab systems, destruction systems and loot tables on Fab only as separate generic pieces, not as a themed valuables kit. Soulslike has two full frameworks (Soulslike Framework, Souls-Like RPG Template) and many dark-fantasy greatsword and cathedral packs, but I found no dedicated art plus Blueprint kit for level mechanics (shortcuts, lifts, portcullis/winch, fog gates) that works with any combat framework. The best openings for our pipeline are therefore hard-surface kits where the 'gameplay-ready function layer' is the product, not the environment. Caveats: fab.com could not be opened, so I saw almost no prices. The only one seen was $24.99, for '90s TVs and VHS Collection', in a snippet. My web search budget ran out before the last 4 verification queries, and itch.io, the Unity Asset Store and mythiclemon.com were blocked.

market_notes.cluster: historical-world (Wild West, pirates/age of sail, Egypt, Rome/Greece, Mesoamerica, Mongol/steppe, Arabian, East Asia, WW1/WW2, Victorian/steampunk)
market_notes.notes: Historical environment kits are saturated in almost every sub-theme. Searches returned 5 or more Fab kits each for Wild West towns (including a free 260-asset Wild West pack covered by DIGITAL PRODUCTION in April 2025), Egyptian temples (Pharaoh's Legacy megapack, Modular Egyptian Temple, Egyptian Pyramid Modular kit), Rome/Greece (Roman City Modular Kit, Roman Pantheon, Roman Empire), Mesoamerica (at least 6 pyramid and temple packs), feudal Japan (Sengoku village, Feudal Japan Megapack, Japanese Mega Bundle, modular castles) and steampunk (several megabundles; Port Aerion seen at $199.99). Epic keeps giving away large historical kits for free (200+ Chinese-architecture pieces in Aug 2025, 80 temple pieces in Jan 2026), which pushes down what buyers pay for plain modular architecture. Korea (hanok kits plus free government-scanned palaces) and the Mongol steppe (2 yurt packs) are small niches, already covered, with low apparent demand. Hero ships and period guns are also well covered: Age of Sail ship collections, a 110+ asset ship package, several animated flintlock/blunderbuss/revolver packs, and mocap animation packs. The thin spots are in the function layer. Themed, working mechanisms came up rarely or not at all: period-styled trap and puzzle devices (the trap packs we found are generic or free tutorial packs), realistic Roman torsion siege engines (the siege packs we found are generic medieval or stylized), a family of rigged horse-drawn wagons, and a modular sailing-ship builder. Synty's Western ($29.99), Samurai ($29.99) and Pirate ($49.99) packs on the Unity store show steady demand for these themes. Our edge is hard-surface parts rigged as separate moving pieces, with sockets, LODs, UCX collision and recolourable master materials. We should sell mechanisms and gameplay-ready devices, not more town or temple architecture.

The first-person retail/job simulator wave that Supermarket Simulator started (Feb 2024) is still producing clones on Steam in 2025: Mall Simulator 2025, Liquor Store Simulator, Wild West Supermarket Simulator and Waterpark Simulator all appeared in search results. A PC Gamer forum post credits part of the flood to a shared retail engine for Unity, which suggests buyers want ready-made kits. On Fab the obvious parts of this genre are crowded. Supermarket environments and fixture kits are well covered (Supermarket; Build-your-own Supermarket with 161 meshes and 34 Blueprints; Grocery store with 900+ prefabs; Modular Convenience Store with 220+ items; Stylized Corner Store; Lowpoly Supermarket). So are Blueprint shop-sim templates (Shop Sim, Replicated Store Simulator Template, Supermarket Simulator Template, Grand Opening, Ultimate Supermarket Shelf Stocking System, TCG Card Store Template). Cozy/cartoon interiors are saturated (Cozy Cartoon Rooms 1 and 2 at 635-670 assets each, several cozy furniture packs, low-poly office packs including Synty POLYGON Office). So are farming (Ultimate Farming with 42 crops, Hyper Farming System v4, several low-poly farm environments), fast-food and kitchen packs, and laundromats (6+ listings). Thin spots appear where a sim needs many small, interchangeable hard-surface parts rather than a finished room. We found PC hardware only as whole-PC models or case packs, with no socketed modular parts kit. TCG/collectibles shop props appear only as one Blueprint template and single booster-pack mockups. Supermarket products exist only as fixed item sets, not as a label-swappable parametric packaging system. Our strengths (sockets, rigid-part rigs, recolourable master materials, LODs, UCX) fit these part-heavy niches better than soft cozy furniture or organic crops. We saw no Fab prices or review counts in snippets, apart from one 4.6 rating on Stylized Farm.

The generic Blueprint gameplay systems are heavily saturated on Fab. One query each returned 7+ inventory systems (Inventory System, Inventory System Fully Blueprint V1.5, Advanced/Complete/RPG/Generic Inventory System), 8+ door/lock/keycard systems (Doors System, Universal Doors System, Keycard System, Hyper Lock and Lockpicking v3, Password Lock System), 4+ Chaos destruction systems (Chaos Prop Destruction System, DENT Chaos, Destruction System), 7 trap packs (including a free 15-trap Assortment of Traps) and 10 modular sword builders (one advertises 331,776 variations). Loot chests and crates, supermarket-sim props and systems, workshop tool packs, warehouse kits, cable/spline tools, spark VFX packs and sci-fi and wood trim sheets all return many listings, so a new generic entry in any of them would need a strong twist. The thin areas are disassembly-ready mechanical assemblies: two Fab-focused queries for engine or mechanic-sim part kits found no Fab listing, only Sketchfab-store engines and Unity items. Safes and vaults also have only a handful of listings (Interactive Safe, Working Safes Minigame, a 5-safe Safe Pack), and rule-driven PCG fills for industrial racking turned up nothing, although the racking meshes themselves are common. Demand signals include Unity sellers making two separate mechanic-sim icon packs, the UE-built mechanic sim Wrench getting an Epic interview, many store-simulator frameworks on Fab, and many lock and puzzle templates showing buyers pay for interactable function. Our Reddit and top-seller searches returned no useful best-seller data, so sales ranks and review counts are "not seen" unless quoted. The best fit for our pipeline is hard-surface rigid-part assemblies with sockets and UCX, sold with a small data-driven Blueprint or PCG function layer. That differentiates us in crowded categories and targets the thin ones directly.

verdicts.notes: Searches ran normally. The siege-engine category on Fab is crowded: at least 5 animated or Blueprint siege packs, including one built from historical data and replicas and a Blueprint ballista. No Roman-specific realistic torsion set (scorpio, cheiroballistra, onager, testudo ram) surfaced, so the narrow gap is real but thin. Demand is the weak point. Many buyers will accept a generic 'ballista' or 'catapult' in a Roman scene; historically exact Roman torsion engines serve a small niche (Total War-like strategy, documentaries or edu viz). The Roman/Greek environment kits on Fab show the setting sells, but sales numbers were not seen. For this to sell: make historical accuracy the headline (cite sources, crew sockets, a working windlass and torsion rigs); bundle crew-free animations and a firing BP that feel better than existing packs; target the Rome/Greece environment buyers with matching materials; price modestly. Better still, fold it into a wider 'Roman Legion camp and field' set rather than selling siege engines alone.
